question: The nonzero coefficients of a polynomial \(P\) with real coefficients are all replaced by their mean to form a polynomial \(Q.\) Which of the following could be a graph of \(y = P(x)\) and \(y = Q(x)\) over the interval \(-4 \le x \le 4?\)
solution:
The mean preserves the total of the numbers being averaged. To connect that fact to the graphs, evaluate the polynomials at \(x=1\): every power of \(1\) equals \(1\), so a polynomial's value there is the sum of its coefficients.

Suppose \(P\) has \(n\geq 1\) nonzero coefficients \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\), with mean
\[
m=\frac{a_1+\cdots+a_n}{n}.
\]
The replacement keeps the same powers of \(x\), leaves zero coefficients unchanged, and replaces each of these \(n\) coefficients by \(m\). Consequently,
\[
P(1)=a_1+\cdots+a_n=nm=Q(1).
\]
This remains true if \(m=0\). Thus the two graphs must have the same height at \(x=1\).

In choices A, C, D, and E, the purple curve is above the black curve at \(x=1\), so those choices are impossible. In choice B, the curves meet at \(x=1\). The answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
